newsitem.title: USA: Defense Secretary's brother cleared in shooting.
newsitem.headline: Defense Secretary's brother cleared in shooting.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen's brother acted in self-defence when he shot a man who was allegedly attempting to rob him, authorities said Friday.

Prosecutors charged Michael Chasse, 22, John Pettegrow Jr., 19, and Kim "Randy" Snow, 16, in connection with an altercation Tuesday night at Robert Cohen's home in nearby Brewer in which Chasse was shot twice in the neck.

"At this point the evidence that we have indicates that these three individuals conspired with one another to rob Mr. Cohen of money, jewelry and other valuables," Penobscot County District Attorney Christopher Almy said.

Almy said the evidence indicated Cohen, 51, William Cohen's younger brother, was "legally justified in using the deadly force that he did use against an armed intruder who was apparently attacking him."
Chasse, of Bangor, was convicted in 1996 in Lewiston of threatening and harassement and Cohen's family and friends claimed after the shooting that Chasse had been stalking Cohen for several weeks.
Chasse, who is listed in good condition at the Eastern Maine Medical Centre in Bangor, was charged with assault, robbery and conspiracy. Pettegrow and Snow were charged with robbery and conspiracy.
The arrest warrant said the three drove to Cohen's house and Chasse attempted to force his way inside with a knife. His two partners allegedly fled when the shots were fired.
Pettegrow has confessed but Snow has denied involvement and Chasse has refused to talk, according to police, who have a witness who allegedly overheard the men planning the crime.

In an interview published Friday morning, Chasse denied attacking Cohen or having a knife. "I went there as a friend," he told the Portland Press Herald in a bedside interview published before the charges were filed.

Cohen's relatives and friends told reporters that Chasse, who was also a friend of Cohen's daughter, had previously tried to intimidate Cohen with demands for money and that Cohen had expressed a fear for his life."
"Bobby Cohen has been through hell," Bobby Russell, a longtime friend of Cohen, told the Press Herald.
